newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam to stick with refinery location plan.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam to stick with refinery location plan.

text.p: Petrovietnam will stick with its original plan to build an oil refinery in the central province of Quang Ngai and will not consider other location proposals, company officials said on Wednesday.
"Economists and technicians can propose anything they want," Ho Si Thoang, chairman of the state oil and gas firm's management board told reporters at a trade fair. "It will be at Dung Quat."

He was responding to a question about a proposal to build two smaller plants, one in the north and one in the south, whose combined capacity would be equivalent to the 6.5 million tonnes per year planned for the Dung Quat plant in Quang Ngai.

On Tuesday Tran Quan Ngoc, the Ministry of Planning and Investment's General Director in charge of foreign investment in southern Vietnam, said such a proposal had been made by experts and that it was likely to be considered by the government.

"In our country there are different opinions on this," Ngoc told reporters on the sidelines of an oil, gas and petrochemicals conference. "And some scientists and economy experts are selling this idea to the government. I think our government will consider it."

However, he noted that a decision had already been taken to press on with construction of a $1.3 billion refinery at Dung Quat, an undeveloped area 1,000 km (600 miles) north of the country's oilfields and chief consumption base.

A consortium of foreign companies which had planned to build the Dung Quat refinery with Vietnam broke up earlier this year after Petrovietnam rejected their demand for greater commercial and financial incentives.
The consortium had been put together to replace France's Total, which walked away from the project in 1995 after deciding that the location made it "economically unviable".

Thoang said Petrovietnam was leaving the door open for foreign partners and noted that talks were continuing with South Korea's LG Group and Malaysia's state oil firm Petroliam Nasional Berhad (Petronas).
"LG and Petronas are old partners, so of course we are discussing it with them," he said.
A source at LG, who declined to be named, confirmed that the company remained in talks on the refinery and said a decision on whether it gets involved would be made within a few months.
